```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.align = "center")

# 30-60-90 reference triangle: short leg x (vertical), long leg x*sqrt(3), hypotenuse 2x
draw_306090 <- function() {
  par(mar = c(1.5, 1.5, 0.5, 1.5))
  s <- sqrt(3)
  plot(NA, xlim = c(-0.3, s + 0.3), ylim = c(-0.25, 1.15), asp = 1,
       axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  polygon(c(0, s, 0), c(0, 0, 1), lwd = 2)
  rect(0, 0, 0.12, 0.12)                                  # right-angle mark
  text(-0.12, 0.5, expression(italic(x)))                 # short leg
  text(s / 2, -0.15, expression(italic(x) * sqrt(3)))     # long leg
  text(s / 2 + 0.15, 0.62, expression(2 * italic(x)))     # hypotenuse
  text(s - 0.38, 0.08, expression(30 * degree), cex = 0.8)
  text(0.16, 0.72, expression(60 * degree), cex = 0.8)
}
```

## 1. Rationalizing denominators

\begin{framed}
\textbf{Goal:} Rewrite a fraction so there is no square root in the denominator. Multiplying the {\bf top and bottom} by the same thing multiplies by 1, so the value does not change.

\textbf{Simple square root in denominator:} Multiply by that square root. \quad
$\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}} \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{6\sqrt{3}}{3} = 2\sqrt{3}$

\textbf{A sum or difference:} Multiply by the \textbf{conjugate}, which flips the sign between the terms. It works because $(a + \sqrt{b})(a - \sqrt{b}) = a^2 - b$, which has no square root.

$\dfrac{8}{3 + \sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{8}{3 + \sqrt{5}} \cdot \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{5}}{3 - \sqrt{5}} = \dfrac{8(3 - \sqrt{5})}{9 - 5} = 2(3 - \sqrt{5}) = 6 - 2\sqrt{5}$
\end{framed}

Rationalize each denominator and simplify.

\vspace{0.3cm}
(a) $\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{6}}$ \hspace{4cm} (b) $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3} - 1}$ \hspace{4cm} (c) $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{2+\sqrt{5}}$

\vfill



## 2. Scaling a vector

\begin{framed}
\textbf{Length:} The vector $[a, b]$ has length $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$.

\textbf{Length 1:} Divide each component by the length. \quad \textbf{Length $k$:} Multiply the length-1 vector by $k$. \quad \textbf{Opposite direction:} Use $-k$.

\textbf{Example:} $[1, 1]$ has length $\sqrt{2}$. Same direction, length 1: $\left[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right] = \left[\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}, \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right]$.
Opposite direction, length 6: $\left[\frac{-6}{\sqrt{2}}, \frac{-6}{\sqrt{2}}\right] = \left[-3\sqrt{2}, -3\sqrt{2}\right]$.
\end{framed}

Given the vector $[2, 1]$, find each vector. Rationalize any denominators.

## 3. The 30-60-90 triangle

\begin{framed}
\textbf{Ratio:} In a 30-60-90 triangle, the sides are $x$ (opposite $30^\circ$), $x\sqrt{3}$ (opposite $60^\circ$), and $2x$ (the hypotenuse).

\textbf{Example:} If the long leg is 6, then $x\sqrt{3} = 6$, so $x = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{3}$, and the hypotenuse is $2x = 4\sqrt{3}$.
\end{framed}

```{r tri, fig.width=3, fig.height=1.7}
draw_306090()
```
